newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -FTSE may extend gains to about 4,760.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -FTSE may extend gains to about 4,760.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index may strengthen to about 4,760 on Wednesday, technical analaysts said.

The index has raced up 182 points or four percent over the past five days but market feelings of weariness or lack of motivation will be banished following a record closing high on Tuesday as investors continue their buying spree.
Most banks, utilities and media stocks will be on their shopping list, while pharmaceuticals may give a mixed performance, analysts added.
By 0722 GMT, at the pre-market open the FTSE was indicated up 4.2 at 4,743.8.

Analysts concede that the rate of rise by the FTSE has been steep recently but its short-term momentum shows no signs of faltering just yet so that by this measure of market dynamics there is still more room for the FTSE to gallop ahead, near-term.

Signs of exhaustion will be recognised when the market starts to make shorter daily advances or volatility decreases. But this alone will not be enough to suggest a severe market correction because it may be that the bull trend will broaden to the smaller capitalised stocks which have not enjoyed the same degree of interest as the top UK 100 companies.

Another sign of a change in trend will be if more frequent market dips occur owing to profit-taking. It may then take several weeks for prices to change course because investors who have missed out on the current rally will be waiting to buy on any setbacks.

In this instance, analysts said a failure by the market to make a further push to higher ground will be met by more concentrated selling and this will overpower any secondary buying pressure coming from these late buyers.
